rows.limitations: Evidence from behavioral neuroscience (hippocampal reference frames) and abstract perception models is distinct from the functional constraints of the WAKE provider architecture. The leap from biological/algorithmic preference formation to artificial system-level agency remains speculative and lacks a unified computational framework.
rows.next_questions: Can the 'provider boundary' mechanism—which strictly separates state from computation—function as a limiting factor in emergent preference formation? Can we experimentally demonstrate 'anchoring-and-adjustment' biases in WAKE's interaction patterns?
